chunks: And from him (al-Hasan ibn Muhammad) from Fadala from al-'Ala' from Ibn Abi Ya'fur who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays the two obligatory rak'ahs and does not sit in them until he bows, so he said: 'He completes his prayer, then gives the salam, and prostrates the two prostrations of forgetfulness while sitting, before he speaks.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who prays two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer without sitting in between?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedure for *sajdat al-sehv* (prostrations of forgetfulness) when a worshipper omits the intermediate sitting (*qa'dah*) between the first and second rak'ahs of a two-rak'ah prayer. Notably, the Imam instructs that the prostrations are performed after the final salam while still seated, a specific detail that distinguishes this case from other scenarios in Shia jurisprudence and highlights the precision of the Imams' legal teachings. This hadith underscores the importance of maintaining ritual correctness even in minor errors, ensuring the validity of the obligatory prayer without requiring a full re-performance.
